ask.text: Tumhare ghar mein kaunsi cheez kilogram mein tolte hain?

body.teacherOpening: Namaste Riya, aaj hum grams aur kilograms seekhenge. Tumhare ghar mein kaunsi cheez kilogram mein tolte hain?

move.shape: greet Riya by name, warm and unhurried; one line on today's topic (Grams and kilograms); then one easy question about them; address them with tum forms (tum, tumhara, tumne), never tu

transcription.prompt: A young child aged 6 to 9 in India answers a teacher aloud in Hindi, English, or a Hindi-English mix. Write Hindi words in Devanagari and English words in Latin script, exactly as spoken.

move.shape: they asked for a photo of एक: there is no photo, say so in a few plain words; the board draws a simple sketch of it instead; describe एक in words they can picture (shape, colour, where it is found), two short sentences; never send their eyes to the screen or the board; then one small question that brings them back to today's idea; never send them to search for it elsewhere; address them with tum forms (tum, tumhara, tumne), never tu; they asked to see एक: say in plain words what it looks like; the board draws what they asked for beside your words: say in plain words what it shows (its parts, its numbers); never send their eyes to the screen or the board, never say it is already there, never that you cannot draw, never ask them to draw it
move.must: never say there is no picture, never draw with characters; if the screen has it, first send their eyes there (dekho / look) and say what to see; if not, paint it in words

ask.text: Use grams ya kilograms mein tolte hain—tum kya bologi?

body.teacherReply: Photo nahi hai; ek aam peela, andaakar hota hai aur ped par milta hai. Use grams ya kilograms mein tolte hain—tum kya bologi?
